title: Conserve mechanical energy
target: Track kinetic and potential energy when nonconservative work is negligible.
criteria: Identify the energy system and assumptions.
Keep the total energy consistent between positions.
Explain how height and speed trade off.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A falling ball has negligible air resistance. Which system includes gravitational potential energy internally?
options: Only the ball, with Earth excluded and gravity ignored.
cpa.guide: Gravitational potential energy belongs to the interacting ball-Earth system.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A cart rolls down a track with substantial friction. Which claim needs correction?
options: K + U is necessarily constant for the cart-Earth system.
A system boundary must be specified.
Total energy is conserved when all forms and transfers are counted.
cpa.guide: Mechanical energy can decrease when friction converts it to internal energy.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.

cpa.prompt: An ideal system has total mechanical energy 46 J and potential energy 17 J. What is kinetic energy?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A frictionless object starts with K = 9 J and U = 25 J. Later U = 14 J. What is later K?
cpa.guide: Total energy is 34 J; later K = 34 − 14 = 20 J.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A point mass starts from rest and falls vertically 1.8 m without resistance. Use g = 10 m/s². What is its speed?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Two point masses of different masses start from rest and descend equal vertical heights on frictionless tracks. Which is true?
options: Path length alone determines final speed.
Both must have equal kinetic energy.
They reach equal speeds even though their kinetic energies can differ.
The heavier one always has twice the speed.
cpa.guide: Mass cancels in v² = 2gΔh; K still scales with mass.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.
